description: Execute a same-history sequence: A obtains term-2 vote at V; B obtains a term-3 majority from A+self without V, appends its no-op and replicates to V; B later attempts term-4 vote at V with candidate-key success or injected unchanged-key failure; A electSelf produces a term-4 stale request. Observe whether V grants A, and all intermediate stored vote keys.

harness.description: Three bootstrapped real Raft states; actual electSelf, requestVote, dispatchLogs, replicateTo and appendEntries. Synchronous transport substitutes RPC scheduling while preserving actual requests/responses.
semantic_changes: No target source edits. skipStartup suppresses background loops; driver schedules campaigns and state transitions serially.

A term-2 election result is collected by the driver but its main-loop majority transition is delayed; B term-3 request reaches A while A is still Candidate, causing the real higher-term handler transition.

B majority transition is performed by the driver after observed A+self grants. Driver initializes one replication state matching startStopReplication and uses actual dispatchLogs/replicateTo for the term-3 no-op.

After the no-op replication, the driver lets the configured lease interval expire, invokes actual checkLeaderLease, performs the sourced runLeader-exit last-contact update and runs actual runFollower to its candidate transition. The enclosing runLeader cleanup is not executed; no prior replication worker remains running.
Transport replaces delivery with synchronous processRPC calls and explicit omissions; each candidate request comes from electSelf. No reply is forged.
StableStore wrapper returns one candidate-key Set error without changing the key; all other writes delegate to InmemStore. Successful-write control uses the same history without that error.

legality.derivation: Bootstrap creates a fixed three-voter configuration. Actual A term-2 campaign saves A at V. B term-3 wins A+self while V delivery is omitted; therefore V need not have voted for B to legally receive B history. Actual dispatchLogs creates the higher-term no-op and replicateTo/appendEntries stores it at V while A remains behind. A learned term 3 by granting B and later electSelf advances it to 4 using its actual old last-log tuple. B term-4 request has the fresh tuple; the failed candidate-key write leaves old A with successfully stored term 4. The driver invokes checkLeaderLease after configured contact expiry, then actual runFollower reaches Candidate on its heartbeat timeout. It substitutes enclosing leader-loop cleanup, performing its last-contact update; this does not alter V vote memory or supply the tested grant. Individual successful stable writes remain intact, and the failed Set returns an ordinary error without corruption. The driver does not fake a prior same-term grant: history of actual V responses is inspected at final admission.
legality.applicability: Local RequestVote freshness after a partial vote persistence error, plus same-sequence successful-write control. Fixed IDs/addresses, no concurrent node mutation during each phase.
alternatives: Actual lease checking and follower timeout execute, but the driver replaces enclosing runLeader setup/cleanup and final majority handling; no stale leader election endpoint is claimed.
Storage backends that stop the process instead of returning the injected error do not exercise this conditional continuation.

grounding.derivation: Admission independently computes log staleness from actual request and receiver log tuples and checks actual prior V response history for same candidate/term grant. Compare the subsequent actual Granted response with false. Distinct operation names correlate each control/discriminator prefix, admission and completed reply. The result is emitted even when granted, not filtered by expected outcome.
grounding.applicability: A log-stale request without previous same-term grant; fault branch has the documented partial pair and successful control has the other candidate saved.

observable_properties.description: The stale candidate without a previous same-term grant must be denied; a new term paired with an old candidate after Set failure cannot serve as an eligibility exception.

uncertainties: No particular production storage backend is exercised; the error-return model is explicit.
Actual election RPC producers, log replication, lease checking and follower timeout execute; enclosing loop setup/cleanup and majority transitions remain driver-controlled.
No final stale-leader election or loss of a committed command is observed.
